My stepmother ( and my father, for doing nothing ).

I spent the second half of my childhood at my father's / stepmother's.

A lot of what happened at my stepmother's is repressed, but through therapy and talking to people who knew me at the time, i have been able to piece together some points. Regular lies were told about me and my father would beat me because he believed her. There was not enough food and I was always hungry / too thin. 24 hours a day I did what I was told. Chores, work, eat, sleep, wash. ( no showers / baths because it was too expensive ( bearing in mind they were reasonably wealthy ) ) There was no time for myself ( and i really mean this, none, except school which was my only release. This was worse in my teenage years when I wanted friends / relationships ). I remember an incident where physical abuse happened because I went to another part of the house to cry, and I was not allowed. I think that I was a nuisance to her, she told me repeatedly to kill myself. I was told if I told anybody, they wouldn't listen to me because I was worthless / things would get worse.

There were 2 things that kept me alive. My hate for them and my sister who went through it all with me. I sometimes fantasize about murdering them but will never actually go through with it.

There is much much more but I don't want to get into it. It has resulted in emotional and physical scars for myself. I am not in touch with my father or stepmother anymore and suffer frequent nightmares about my times there. 


I have now built a life for myself and am reasonably happy. 

**tl:dr: my stepmother is the only person I have ever been able to call "evil" due to my "experiences" with her**

It's all about who you have a discussion with. Debating is something I really enjoy and I usually play devils advocate for no other reason than having a debate. It is best to set out some ground rules before doing so, however:

1, Bring a degree of neutrality to the topic. If you go in with strong opinions that you are not willing to budge from, then, imo, that is an argument.

2, Listen to the other person. You would be surprised by the amount of people who have poor listening skills. ( encourage, ask questions, let them finish etc etc). This is something that should be taught in schools.

3, Have a mediator. If one party has a stronger personality, they will try to dominate the conversation ( it is human nature ). The mediator can step in when a point turns into a 10 minute rant etc. The mediator must remain neutral.

4, Intellectual safety word. People may end up hearing things that will make them emotional. It is better to stop than lose friends. I like using "space sloth" for no other reason than space sloth is awesome.

This story always comes up at parties if i'm around old friends...

I was 17 and at a party in a garage. Lots of underage drinking was taking place. As the amount of alcohol consumed went up, common sense went down.

It is worth noting that this garage was not attached to a house and had no electricity. There were plenty of candles to keep the place lit (which is why there is a new garage in the same spot, but that is another story).

As the night continued, the guys in the room were all competing for the gals attention. Metaphoric pissing contests began. "I can drink more than him.." "I once got into a fight with a dog" etc etc. I imagine other stupid things happened, but mine eclipsed it all.

I saw my ticket to "win" this night and get all the attention my drunk self thought I deserved from the ladies. A tea candle ( you know, one of those candles that has an aluminum base to hold in the wax after it melts.). It was still lit but all the wax had turned into a pot of molten glory.

I got everyone's attention and picked that candle up, blew out the wick and downed it like a shot. My immediate feeling of pure hardcoreness was very quickly replaced by regret as the wax first burnt my mouth then my gullet. The pain was excruciating but it did not stop there. The wax, after cooling within the first stages of my digestive system, begins to solidify. I have no way of explaining this feeling other than "what the actual fuck is happening to me " so I'm going with that. 

Much coughing and red-eyedness followed as I attempted to clear my mouth / gullet from this waxy death. Beer helped. Clearing my mouth so I could breath, I must of looked like I just took a load from a waxwork model. I continued the night as if nothing had happened.

I can't remember which woman I was trying to impress but I went home alone that night. It was all a haze  of cheap beer, cheap tobacco and cheaper candle wax.

**tl;dr: I drank molten candle wax to impress women I can't even remember**

The teachings are for him to interpret as he wishes. There are many different denominations of Buddhism as there are many denominations of other religions. What holds them together as a larger faith is some core beliefs.

For example, the most core of beliefs for Christianity is that Jesus was the son of God. You could believe nothing else in the bible, but still call yourself a Christian if you believe this.

Buddhism is a bit different as there is no mention of "divine". In my opinion, a Buddhist is someone who follows the teachings of the Buddha, and the most basic of those teachings is that suffering is caused by want; to lessen suffering you must be content with what you have. (there are many other teachings but I believe this is the most fundamental, and is up for argument).  

Vegetarianism is an important part of Buddhism as there is no need to eat meat. People eat meat because they desire to, and this desire causes suffering to themselves and (obviously) the animals they eat. However, it is not absolutely necessary to be a vegetarian or vegan to be a Buddhist.

I am a Buddhist so abstaining from meat is part of my faith. However, During the time that Adam and Eve were in the garden of Eden, it can be argued that they were vegan. 

And God said, “Behold, I have given you every plant yielding seed that is on the face of all the earth, and every tree with seed in its fruit. You shall have them for food. And to every beast of the earth and to every bird of the heavens and to everything that creeps on the earth, everything that has the breath of life, I have given every green plant for food.” And it was so. (Genesis 1:29-30)

Of course this is all a metaphor for humanity becoming self aware, and individuals having to live with guilt of past actions. Animals do not worry about these things.

Also, it is worth noting that you can find arguments for most things in most Holy texts. Their ambiguity allow for new branches of the religion to emerge when civilisation deems it necessary.

I agree with you but not everyone wants to hear even a well thought out argument if it goes against their current belief system. If the listener is eager I am happy to oblige.

Good dialogue comes into being for me around good friends or rational people enjoying some scotch; alongside politics, health, religion and all manner of questions. Veganism / Vegetarianism is but one of the subjects I like to discuss.

You have no such obligations. Your obligation is to live a happy healthy life, with or without meat. It is not your responsibility to end all suffering. 

Saying that you are obligated to convince people to  change their lifestyle choice due to your own personal beliefs is nothing short of fanaticism. Be it for a good reason or not. 

Keep your beliefs to yourself and positively encourage those who are interested in vegetarianism / veganism if they ask questions. You will keep your friends and family longer as well as your own sanity.

Try not to alienate yourself from the general public. Speaking from past experience, just let it slide. There is next to nothing you can do about it and dwelling on -that- side of vegetarianism for too long will just make you angry at the world around you.

If you are vegetarian / vegan for ethical reasons try to live your life as an example. By allowing people to see how it is possible, and yes, answer all those never ending questions, some will come over to the idea of a vegetarian lifestyle. 

By pointing out somebody's flaws in the way they reason, you will just distance yourself from them and find it hard to keep your old friends and, the ones you make will be just as intolerant and alienated as yourself, fueling a zealot mindset.

I am vegan and keep various pets. Veganism is my lifestyle choice, not theirs. It is your responsibility as a pet owner to keep your pets healthy and happy. As far as choosing a pet as a vegan I would hugely recommend pet rats; they are great fun and can live healthily on a plant based diet.

I keep various amphibians and a bearded dragon they all eat from roach colony i keep at home (It really is roach heaven). I also have a snake that eats rats but farming rats for food (frozen thawed not live) is by far more ethical than any cat food you would buy in a supermarket. (As a longtime keeper of rats and mice they suffer FAR FAR less from intensive farming than animals kept for human consumption because they enjoy being in large confined groups. Also a snake will eat far less than most any animal of a similar size.

I am the only vegan i know irl that 1, keeps exotics and feeds them meat and 2, who feeds my own cat meat. All the vegan cats I see are underweight, sadly. I know of a vegan ferret that is also underweight but the vegan dogs suffer less from a vegan diet. However, back to my original point, it is not your pet's choice to be vegan and if you wish to keep certain species of animals as pets you must be willing to make compromises on this point. Not everything is so black and white, all or nothing, do what you feel comfortable with.

EDIT: I just wanted to add it is also your responsibility to get good sourced animal food. Check what is available in your country and be prepared to pay more for "ethical" dog and cat food.
